faq_logTimeReminders_q: Can WitnessWork remind me to log time for a day I planned?
faq_logTimeReminders_a: Yes. Go to Preferences → Plans, turn on Remind Me to Log Time, and choose a Remind At time (8:00 PM unless you change it). If a day has a plan but no time logged, you get one reminder at that time after the day's plans end: a morning plan reminds you that evening, and a plan still going at your Remind At time reminds you the next day. Several plans on the same day give one reminder, and when two days' reminders would arrive at the same time they're combined. Logging any time for that day stops its reminder and clears one you've already received; removing that day's plans or turning the setting off does too. A day planned with no time doesn't remind you, and days you missed before turning the setting on aren't included. Tapping the reminder opens Add Time with the date, planned time, and type already filled in. The reminder is also listed in the Home bell for a week, even if system notifications are off. The setting appears when you track hours; Regular Publishers turn on Log my hours first. Turning it on asks for notification permission, or opens your device settings if you've declined before. Reminders are worked out on your device from your own plans and time and aren't sent anywhere. Each device schedules its own reminders up to two weeks ahead, so open WitnessWork at least every two weeks to keep them coming. If you log time on another device, open WitnessWork on this one so it can cancel that day's reminder. On Android, the system may deliver a reminder a few minutes late to save battery. If reminders don't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.
faq_navigationShortcuts_q: How do I navigate with keyboard shortcuts on iPad?
faq_navigationShortcuts_a: Connect a hardware keyboard to an iPad running iPadOS 26 or later, then hold Command while the main navigation is visible. Small shortcut labels appear beside the bottom tabs or sidebar items. Press Command and the displayed number to open that screen; release Command to hide the labels. Numbers follow the visible navigation order, so Home is Command 1, Schedule is Command 2, and Contacts is Command 3. Other numbers depend on which items are visible, including Settings in the sidebar. Close any open form or other screen before using these navigation shortcuts; they do not save or discard records. Only shortcut use is measured, not what you type. Support requires an installed app build with the keyboard feature and is unavailable on iPhone and Android. If labels do not appear, check that the keyboard is connected, return to the main navigation, and update and reopen the app. You can always tap navigation items instead. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep contact details out of public reports.

faq_pointerHover_q: How do I use a trackpad, mouse, or Apple Pencil on iPad?
faq_pointerHover_a: Connect a trackpad or mouse to your iPad, or hover a supported Apple Pencil just above the screen. Buttons, rows, and calendar days highlight as the pointer moves over them. When the sidebar is narrowed to icons, resting the pointer on an icon shows its name; other icon-only buttons, such as the map controls and Notifications, also show their names. Hover over the activity grid, the Service Year pace chart, or a mileage bar to see its date and value. On the map, hover a pin to see the contact's name, or hover a contact in the map's side list to name its pin. A secondary click (two-finger click) opens the same menu and preview as touching and holding. The sidebar's resize bar shows arrows for the directions it can still move, and two-finger scrolling moves a contact photo while you crop it. Everything is still available by touch: tap, touch and hold, or drag as usual. Hover changes nothing in your records. Only the fact that a pointer or Pencil was used is measured, at most once a day; no positions, names, or values are sent. On Android, a mouse highlights rows and shows names and chart values, but pins on the map don't show names on hover. iPhone has no hover. If nothing responds, check that the trackpad, mouse, or Pencil is connected, then update and reopen the app. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep contact details out of public reports.
faq_menuBar_q: How do I use the menu bar on iPad?
faq_menuBar_a: On iPadOS 26 or later, use Windowed Apps or Stage Manager and swipe down from the top edge to reveal the menu bar. After setup, WitnessWork Preferences opens in-app settings; the standard Settings item opens your device's settings. File opens Add Time when hours logging is enabled, Add Contact, New Plan, and Backup & Restore. Edit → Find Contact opens the Contacts list and focuses search. Help opens the Help Center, What's New, your email app for private support, or Check for Update. These shortcuts reuse the existing screens; opening a form does not save or share your records. Check for Update checks for a compatible app update and uses the existing download and restart flow when one is available. It cannot install a new native app version, and is unavailable in development builds. Menu-bar support requires an installed app build that includes it and is unavailable on iPhone and Android. If items are missing, update from your app store and reopen WitnessWork. You can still use the same actions inside the app. For other problems, use the Help Center's private email link and keep contact details and backups out of public reports.

1320.c4: 'Add Time' screen now allows for increments of 1 minute.
1320.c5: Added Kinyarwanda language, fully translated by Semana D. Thank you so much for your help!
1320.c6: You can now select how your time is displayed. Choose between decimal like: 13.5 or choose 13 Hrs 30 Mins. Visit Preferences > Appearance.

1330.c1: Added language selector. See Preferences to manually adjust your language.
1330.c2: Resolved issue with one-time plan having an inaccurate maximum date.

1340.c1: Added a special reward for when you check off your time box or add time!
1340.c2: You can now set a decimal value for hour goals on 'custom' publisher type.

1350.c1: You can now use autocomplete to search for an address! Just start typing to see suggestions. This feature is only possible by your generous donations. Thank you for your support!
1350.c2: Resolved issue where day sheet would not close automatically when adding time to a day of month.
1350.c3: Resolved overflow issue on home screen for tablets.

1360.c1: New: Share Contacts and easily import them. Transferring calls is now easier than ever.
1360.c2: You can now customize the colors of the pins on the map.
1360.c3: New: Dismiss Contact feature. You can now dismiss contacts you no longer wish to visit and receive notifications when it's time to return to them.
1360.c4: Added notes support to time reports.
1360.c5: Enhanced recurring plan scheduling - You can now schedule plans monthly by day of week (e.g., 'first Monday of every month').
1360.c7: Added statistics sections to your Monthly and Yearly reports to better track your progress and patterns.
1360.c8: You can now change your calendar's first day of the week. Visit Preferences > Appearance.
1360.c10: Follow up topic now supports multiple lines.
1360.c11: There are now no restrictions on when you can add time or schedule plans.
1360.c12: Added visual indicators on calendar days to show when notes are present.
1360.c13: Resolves issue with Korean and Panama phone number formatting.
1360.c14: Contact Details Screen map is now zoomed out to easily see surroundings at a glance.
1360.c15: Fixed various navigation issues when adding time and scheduling plans.
1360.c16: Improved readability and consistency throughout the app with better spacing and button sizes.

1382.c1: The Milestone Update is here. A whole new look with a floating tab bar, frosted cards, and a fresh, modern feel throughout the app.
1382.c2: New Contacts tab with fuzzy search, smart sort, and stacked filters. Your contacts are now a first-class destination.
1382.c3: Progress Screen 2.0: a fresh look at Month, Year, and All-time, with customizable milestones, category breakdowns, and lifetime hours.
1382.c4: iCloud sync arrives (Supporter): your reports, contacts, and plans stay in step across all your devices. Optional photo sync keeps avatars synced too.
1382.c5: Onboarding has been rebuilt from the ground up. A personal note from the developer, animated plan previews, and a checklist tailored to your goals.
1382.c6: Brand new home screen widgets: month calendar, appointments, hours, and contacts. All one tap away.
1382.c7: Contact avatars are here. Photos or emoji, with a tap-to-expand fullscreen viewer.
1382.c8: Share a contact with another publisher via secure universal links.
1382.c9: Smarter recurring plans. Schedule by day-of-week and week-of-month, with per-instance overrides and deletions.
1382.c10: Time rollover: fractional minutes carry forward into the next month, manually or automatically.
1382.c11: Beautiful new celebrations the moment you cross a goal.
1382.c12: New Supporter tier with personalization, including a custom accent color.
1382.c13: Schedule screen: a focused calendar view of day plans and recurring conversations.
1382.c14: A redesigned profile card on the home screen showing your role, time served, and fun stats.
1382.c15: Approaching and missed conversations now surface on the home screen so you never lose track.
1382.c16: Phone region code now persists across new contacts. Phone region search is faster and more accurate.
1382.c17: Map empty state, location prompts, and contact map clustering have all been polished.
1382.c18: Countless small bug fixes, performance improvements, and visual refinements throughout the app.

1383.c1: Plans now have a Type. Assign a category to a scheduled plan and your projected totals reflect the right kind of credit.
1383.c2: Projected totals are more accurate. They respect your monthly credit cap and no longer double-count time you've already logged today.
1383.c3: The celebration chime once again respects your ring/silent switch.
1383.c5: New contacts and address edits now save immediately, even before the geocode api finishes locating them.
1383.c6: The calendar refreshes right away after you add, edit, or remove a plan.
1383.c7: Map pins stay in focus after you tap them. Resolve intermittent issue with map refocusing incorrect contact pin.
1383.c8: Smoother scrolling in the Contacts list. Resolve issues with contacts disappearing.
1383.c4: Your Donations now shows the correct billing period and price for annual and granted supporter subscriptions.

1400.c1: Switching from MyTime? You can now import your contacts and visit history straight from a MyTime backup, with a preview before anything is added, so there's no manual re-entry.
1400.c2: Date format, clock style, and start of the week are now separate from your app language. Set each one in Settings > Date & Time, with an Auto option that follows your region or device.
1400.c3: You can now customize the day thresholds and colors behind contact staleness. Tune them in Settings > Personalization > Color Key.
1400.c4: Resolved an issue with the map search auto closing.
1400.c5: Locating contacts on the map now shows live progress, and you can skip it midway without losing your place.
1400.c6: Faster, smoother scrolling in the Contacts list, plus quicker home screen widget updates.
1400.c7: Fixed projected totals around time zone changes, enlarged header buttons for easier tapping, and polished countless small details throughout the app.

1411.c1: New: Meet Scribe AI. Paste your field-ministry notes, whether a handwritten-style log or an export from another app, and Scribe AI turns them into contacts, visits, and time entries for you to review before anything is saved. Refine the results by chatting inline, start an import right from onboarding, and never lose a credit on an import that finds nothing.
1411.c2: A new customizable This Month dashboard on the home screen. Your goal, projection, and schedule pace live in cards you can arrange and expand, while your Service Report stays in one clean card. Tap the report for a full breakdown.
1411.c3: Monthly goal overrides. Set a different goal for a single month when your circumstances change, and see your planned hours as their own progress ring.
1411.c4: Plan more than one thing per day. Day plans on the same date now add together, each keeping its own category, and plans that do not count toward a day are clearly marked.
1411.c5: Easier editing everywhere. Plans, time entries, and conversations now have an ellipsis menu for Edit and Delete, and recurring plans offer clear choices for changing one date, future dates, or the whole series.
1411.c6: Service Reports: Hourglass and NW Publisher submission are back, you can pick a default submission method, edit the report comment before sending, and get a month-end reminder. The year-by-year history can now be trimmed or backfilled with earlier years.
1411.c7: Schedule now shows each day's status at a glance: ahead, behind, on track, upcoming, matched, or no plan.
1411.c8: Supporter status now follows your Apple ID across devices, Scribe AI allowances roll over on a schedule, and the Supporter screen has been simplified.
1411.c9: Fixed time entries and plans landing on the wrong day in time zones at UTC+12 and beyond, plus wrong-day dates late in the evening west of UTC. Fixed map pins opening the wrong contact after swiping the card carousel. Time rollover now keeps Credit Time in its original month by default.
1411.c10: The Credit toggle on categories is now available to every hours-based role. Also fixed a rare crash when closing a picker, restored favorite stars and the current-month Bible study icon, updated to Expo SDK 57, and trimmed the app size.

1420.c1: New iPad layouts show contacts, maps, and schedules alongside their details.
1420.c2: Customize contact fields: reorder phone, email, and custom fields, hide phone or email, and permanently delete archived custom fields.
1420.c3: See your logged time by category across the Service Year, and adjust the monthly credit limit in supported Publisher preferences.
1420.c4: Hourglass submissions now separate preaching time from Credit Time.
1420.c5: The calendar Assistant is available again, with controls in Schedule preferences.

1430.c1: Data protection mode for publishers in the EU, the UK and Switzerland keeps householder records to what the law allows, including consent tracking and cleanup of contacts you haven't visited in a while.
1430.c2: Create a contact right from a pin you drop on the map.
1430.c3: Kingdom Publishers can choose to log their hours with a timer, an optional monthly goal and the Progress tab.
1430.c4: The Year tab now shows your service-year total for every role, even without an annual goal.
1430.c5: Follow-ups on visits are now optional, and you can turn off app sounds in Preferences.
1430.c6: Fixed dates shifting for publishers in far-east time zones.

notesImport_description: Paste field-ministry notes or an export from another app. Scribe AI turns them into Contacts, Visits, and Time Entries for you to review before anything is saved.
notesImport_disclosureTitle: How Scribe AI reads your notes
notesImport_disclosureBody: Scribe AI sends your notes to a third-party language model hosted in a privacy-friendly region under a zero-data-retention agreement. It reads your text and keeps nothing afterward. WitnessWork stores no copy of your notes on our servers, and nothing is added to your records until you review and confirm.

notesImport_privacySummary: Scribe AI sends your notes through OpenRouter to trusted Western language-model providers with Zero Data Retention, so they aren't stored. Notes are held only while the import runs; your history stays on your device. WitnessWork never sells or shares your notes or uses them to train models.

faq_timeRollover_q: Does my time automatically roll over to the next month?
faq_timeRollover_a: Yes. Partial hours below your monthly goal can carry over to the next month. Open Preferences → Publisher and turn on the rollover option. The carried hours appear automatically when the new month begins, so you don't need to manually subtract or re-enter anything.
faq_bibleStudies_a: Studies are tracked per contact, not per day. To count a study, open a contact, log a conversation, and mark it as "Conducted Bible Study." That contact will count as 1 study for the current month, even if you have multiple sessions with them. To raise your study count, mark a study conversation with a different contact.
faq_iCloudSync_q: Can I sync my data between devices?
faq_iCloudSync_a: iCloud Sync is a Supporter feature on iOS. Open Settings → iCloud Sync on each supported device using the same iCloud account to sync your service records, contacts, visits, and preferences. Photos have a separate Include images in sync switch. If a device signs in to a different Apple Account, iCloud Sync turns off there before any records are read or sent, and they stay on the device; turn sync back on to choose how to combine it with that account’s iCloud data. That device also stops sharing Supporter status from your previous account; if it was bought with this device’s App Store account, use Restore Purchases. A device set up from another device’s backup syncs as its own device automatically. Calendar Sync is a separate, free feature that publishes selected Follow-ups to a dedicated calendar; it does not sync your app records between devices. Both features are unavailable on Android; use Settings → Backup & Restore to transfer a saved backup instead.
faq_calendarSetup_q: How do I show Follow-ups in my calendar?
faq_calendarSetup_a: Calendar Sync is free on iOS and isn't available on Android. During first-time setup, or from the invitation in the notifications tray after updating, tap Add to Calendar to create a WitnessWork calendar (in iCloud when available). You can also set it up anytime in Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync: allow full calendar access, then create a WitnessWork calendar or choose a calendar used only for WitnessWork. Updates need iCloud sign-in and an internet connection, even for Google or Outlook calendars. To use Google or Outlook, create a calendar with that provider, add the account in iPhone Settings → Apps → Calendar → Calendar Accounts, and turn on its calendars. Your default calendar and calendars stored only on this device can't be selected. Once a calendar is selected, every upcoming Follow-up is added automatically, including ones you already saved, as a 30-minute event. To leave one out or change its duration, use Show in Calendar in that Follow-up form. To add only the Follow-ups you choose, turn off Add follow-ups automatically, then turn on Show in Calendar for each one. Past Follow-ups, service Plans, and recurring Plans aren't added. Each event gets the same alert as its Follow-up's Notify Me reminder, and no alert when Notify Me is off. Your calendar provider may add its own default alerts; for Google, remove them under that calendar's Event notifications in Google Calendar settings. Make changes in WitnessWork, because calendar edits, including alerts, may be replaced on the next update.
faq_calendarPrivacy_q: What does Calendar Sync share or store?
faq_calendarPrivacy_a: By default, published events contain a generic Follow-up title, the appointment time and duration, and a link that opens the Visit in WitnessWork. Include names and addresses is optional and applies across your devices; turning it on adds those details to published events. Visit notes and Follow-up topics are never exported. Your chosen calendar provider may sync events to other devices, shared calendars, and widgets, so check that calendar's sharing settings before including details. WitnessWork manages only events it marked as its own and does not import your personal calendar appointments. A private iCloud record stores device names and opaque identifiers, publishing ownership, the connected calendar's name and account label, shared options, and event identifiers. Appointment content stays in the chosen calendar account. Each device's calendar identifier and connection state stay local and are separate from app-data sync and backup files.
faq_calendarPrimary_q: Why does Calendar Sync use a primary device?
faq_calendarPrimary_a: Exactly one device publishes your Follow-ups to avoid competing updates. The first device to connect becomes primary. On iOS devices using the same iCloud account, open Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync to register each device, view the Primary device list, and choose a primary. Calendar Sync itself does not require Supporter. Follow-ups edited on another device reach the primary through existing app-data sync, which still requires Supporter and enabled iCloud Sync; open WitnessWork on the primary to publish them. After a transfer, the new primary needs access to the same calendar account and full calendar permission. If a transfer is pending, reopen WitnessWork on the previous primary so it can finish its interrupted operation. There is no automatic timeout takeover if that device is permanently unavailable; use private support under Still need help? in the Help Center. Removing a stale device from the list does not delete its app records or calendar events.
faq_calendarTroubleshooting_q: Calendar events are missing or updates are paused. What should I do?
faq_calendarTroubleshooting_a: Open Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync and read the displayed error. Check your internet connection, iCloud sign-in, calendar account, and full calendar access for WitnessWork in iPhone Settings. Use Sync now on the primary device after your calendar account and app data finish syncing. A missing calendar must be reconnected or replaced; calendars renamed outside WitnessWork may need to be chosen again. When a previously published future event is missing, updates pause even if this device published it: calendar sync delays, deletion, and moving an event can look the same. Wait for the calendar account to finish syncing and confirm you chose the same dedicated calendar. Move any WitnessWork events you moved elsewhere back before retrying. Restore missing events is an explicit recovery option after those checks; it can create duplicates if copies are still downloading or remain elsewhere. A past Follow-up is not initially added. For pending device transfers, reopen the previous primary. If the problem continues, use the Help Center's private support option and include the app version, device and operating-system version, and the error shown. Keep contact details, calendar screenshots, notes, and backups out of public reports.
faq_calendarDisconnect_q: What happens when I disconnect Calendar Sync or uninstall WitnessWork?
faq_calendarDisconnect_a: In Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync, choose Disconnect calendar. Keep events stops publishing on this device and leaves its existing calendar copies. On the primary device, Remove WitnessWork events removes marked events from the selected calendar, including previously exported history; unrelated events and the calendar itself remain. A successful disconnect on the primary also clears the shared destination. Calendar events left by Keep events or uninstalling are no longer maintained until you reconnect. Uninstalling WitnessWork does not remove calendar events. You can remove an unused dedicated calendar in your calendar app after checking that it contains nothing you want to keep. Disconnecting does not delete your Contacts, Visits, or Follow-ups in WitnessWork.
faq_widgets_q: Are there home or lock screen widgets?
faq_widgets_a: Yes, on iOS. Long-press your home or lock screen, tap the + button, search for WitnessWork, and pick the widget you want. The hours widget shows your monthly progress at a glance.
faq_appleWatch_q: Is there an Apple Watch app?
faq_appleWatch_a: Yes, for iPhone with an Apple Watch on watchOS 26 or later. It installs automatically if Automatic App Install is on; otherwise open the Watch app on your iPhone, find WitnessWork under Available Apps, and tap Install. Then open WitnessWork on your iPhone once so your watch gets your progress. On the watch you can add time for today with an optional Type, start and pause your iPhone's timer, and save the timer's time as an entry. If you don't log hours as a Kingdom Publisher, you can mark that you shared the good news this month. To see your hours toward this month's goal, add the Monthly Progress complication to a watch face or your Smart Stack. You can also ask Siri on your watch: "Add time in WitnessWork", "Start my timer in WitnessWork" or "Pause my timer in WitnessWork". Your iPhone keeps your records. The watch only receives your monthly progress, report status, timer and Types, never contacts or notes, and it can't edit or delete entries. The watch app needs your iPhone, so it isn't available on Android or for an Apple Watch set up with Family Setup.
faq_appleWatchSync_q: Why does my Apple Watch say Syncing with iPhone?
faq_appleWatchSync_a: Time you add on your watch is sent to your iPhone right away when it's nearby, or the next time they connect, and saved once WitnessWork runs on your iPhone. Until then your watch shows Syncing with iPhone, and its total doesn't include that time yet. Each entry keeps the day you added it on the watch, is saved only once even if it's sent again, and isn't brought back if you already deleted it on your iPhone. Saved entries reach your other devices with iCloud Sync like any other entry. Starting, pausing and saving the timer need your iPhone nearby. If the watch says the timer changed on your iPhone, check the time and try again. If your watch stays out of date, keep your iPhone nearby and unlocked, open WitnessWork on your iPhone, then open it on your watch. After your iPhone restarts, unlock it once before syncing. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your records out of public reports.
faq_switchingPioneer_q: How do I switch between Publisher and Auxiliary Pioneer mid-month?
faq_switchingPioneer_a: Open Preferences → Publisher Status and choose what fits right now: Publisher, Auxiliary Pioneer, Regular Pioneer, Special Pioneer, Circuit Overseer, or Custom. Goals and totals adjust to match. Switch back when you're done. Past months keep the time you entered, so your history stays accurate.
faq_submitReport_q: Does the app submit my service report for me?
faq_submitReport_a: WitnessWork doesn't send your report anywhere by itself. How and to whom you submit is up to you and your service committee. Open a month's Field Service Report, choose a method from the dropdown above the Submit button, and tap Submit. You can copy a plain-text summary, share it, or hand it straight to Hourglass or NW Publisher, which opens with your hours, Credit, and Bible studies filled in for you to review and send. NW Publisher only accepts the previous month's report. WitnessWork remembers your choice; you can also change it in Preferences → Submission method.
faq_remainingHours_q: How do I see how many hours I have left this month or year?
faq_remainingHours_a: Open the Progress tab from the bottom bar. The Month sub-screen shows time so far and hours left for the current month. Pioneers can switch to the Year sub-screen to see annual goal progress, time so far, remaining hours, and a per-month breakdown comparing actual hours to plan.
faq_goalPacing_q: How can I tell if I'm ahead or behind on my hour goal?
faq_goalPacing_a: Open the Progress tab from the bottom bar. The Month sub-screen shows your daily target so you can see if you're on track for the current month. Pioneers can switch to the Year sub-screen, where the Service Year Pace chart shows how far ahead or behind your Annual Goal you are today, and each month's bar shows how that month did against its goal.
faq_serviceYearPace_q: How do I read the Service Year Pace chart?
faq_serviceYearPace_a: Open the Progress tab and switch to Year. If your status has an Annual Goal, such as regular pioneer, the Service Year Pace card appears below your milestones. The dashed gray line is where your Annual Goal puts you by the end of each month. It is built from each month's own goal, so a mid-year appointment or an auxiliary pioneer month changes it, but a Monthly Goal you changed yourself does not. The green line is your time so far, counted the same way as your Service Report, including each month's credit limit. The dashed green line adds the time you have planned. The faint line is last service year, shown when you logged time in it, and the number at its end is last year's total. If a line runs well past your Annual Goal, the space above the goal is drawn on a compressed (logarithmic) scale so the months below stay readable. Press and hold the chart, then slide your finger, to see any month's totals. "Ahead of pace" compares your time with where the goal line is today. Below the card, each month has a bar: solid for logged time, lighter for credit time, and striped for plans, with a tick at that month's goal. The key above the months explains these marks, and the Hours and vs Goal columns give the numbers. Every bar uses the same scale, so you can compare months. Without an Annual Goal you see the month bars but not the chart. If a month looks wrong, press and hold it to change its status or goal. The chart is drawn on your device from your own entries and isn't shared.
faq_timeFormat_q: Can I display time as "1h 30m" instead of "1.5"?
faq_timeFormat_a: Yes. Open Preferences → Appearance and choose your preferred time format. Both formats are available everywhere time is shown.
faq_weekStart_q: Can I start the week on Monday instead of Sunday?
faq_weekStart_a: Yes. Preferences → Appearance lets you choose the first day of the week. The change applies to the calendar, schedule, and any other weekly views.
faq_darkMode_q: Can I force dark mode or light mode?
faq_darkMode_a: Yes. Open Preferences → Appearance → Color Scheme and pick System, Light, or Dark. The app will stop following your phone's setting and use the one you choose.
faq_appIcon_q: Can I change the app's icon?
faq_appIcon_a: Alternate app icons are a Supporter perk on iOS. Open Settings → Personalization → App Icon and choose an alternate. Alternate app icons are unavailable on Android.
faq_reorderHome_q: Can I reorder the cards on my home screen?
faq_reorderHome_a: Yes. Open Preferences → Home Screen to show, hide, and reorder cards. The home screen will keep your custom layout going forward.
faq_reorderTabs_q: Can I change the order of the tabs?
faq_reorderTabs_a: Yes. Open Settings → Preferences → Tab Order and use the up and down arrows beside each tab, or long-press a tab's name to move it to the top or bottom. The new order applies right away to the bottom bar on phones and the sidebar on tablets, on iOS and Android. Tabs can be reordered but not hidden. WitnessWork still opens on Home, and Progress only appears for roles that log hours; it keeps its place in your order if you change roles. On iPad, Command-number keyboard shortcuts follow your order too. The order is a preference, so it's included in backups and syncs with iCloud when sync is on; it doesn't change any of your records. To go back, move the tabs back to Home, Schedule, Contacts, Progress. If the order doesn't update, restart the app and use Still need help? below.
faq_timerRounding_q: Why was my timer rounded to the nearest 5 minutes?
faq_timerRounding_a: That was old behavior. Recent versions save the exact stopwatch time when you stop the timer, with no rounding. If you're still seeing 5-minute rounding, update the app to the latest version.
faq_addNotesToTime_q: Can I add notes to a time entry?
faq_addNotesToTime_a: Yes. When you add or edit a time entry, you can attach a note (e.g. "cart witnessing" or "cut short"). You can also tag entries with categories so similar entries stay grouped in your time reports.
faq_specialPioneerAnnual_q: I'm a special pioneer, why is the app showing me an annual goal?
faq_specialPioneerAnnual_a: Special pioneers don't have an annual goal by default. If yours appears, open Preferences → Publisher and turn off the annual goal. Your monthly goal stays in place and the annual bar on the Progress tab's Year sub-screen will be hidden.
faq_ldcCreditCap_q: Are LDC and other credit hours included in my totals?
faq_ldcCreditCap_a: Yes. Credit hours count toward your monthly hour total. For the service-year total, up to 55 credit hours per month are counted, in line with the branch's published cap. Anything above the cap is still kept on the entry but doesn't roll into the annual total.
faq_timezoneShift_q: Will my time entries or plans shift days if I travel between timezones?
faq_timezoneShift_a: No. As of the April 2026 update, every time entry and plan is anchored to its calendar date independent of timezone, so traveling or crossing a daylight-saving boundary will not move entries to a different day. Older entries created before that update are migrated automatically the first time you open the new version. If you ever spot an entry on the wrong day after updating, please send a bug report and we'll take a look.
faq_editRecurringPlan_q: Can I edit or delete a single occurrence of a recurring plan?
faq_editRecurringPlan_a: Yes. Open the Schedule tab, tap the day you want to change, and choose "Edit" or "Delete" for that occurrence. Your recurring plan stays intact for every other day.
faq_awayDay_q: How do I mark a day I'm not going out without breaking my recurring plan?
faq_awayDay_a: Tap the day on the Schedule tab and add an override for an "away" or empty day. The override only affects that one day, and the recurring plan keeps going from the next day forward.
faq_importContacts_q: Can I import contacts from my phone's address book?
faq_importContacts_a: Not at this time. Contacts are entered manually in WitnessWork. This keeps your ministry contacts private and avoids accidentally pulling in personal contacts.
faq_importOtherApps_q: Can I import data from MyTime, Ministry Assistant, or another app?
faq_importOtherApps_a: MyTime backups are supported. Open Settings → MyTime Import, choose the original .mytimedb backup from MyTime, and review the preview before importing. Other apps' backup formats are not automatically supported. If you can export readable text, Notes Import may help bring it in with Scribe AI on supported iOS devices when available. Review its proposed records and warnings before saving. WitnessWork JSON backups belong in Settings → Backup & Restore instead.
faq_backupRestore_q: How do I back up and restore my data?
faq_backupRestore_a: Open Settings → Backup & Restore → Create Backup or Restore From Backup to export or restore a JSON backup on iOS or Android. On a new device, you can also choose From a backup file on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen; restoring there finishes setup with your restored profile. Backups include service records, plans, contacts, visits, categories, profile, and shared preferences. A restore replaces the included local data; older backups may omit categories or profile, which are kept as they are. Device identity, iCloud settings, data protection mode, analytics consent, and onboarding progress stay local to this device. Photo files are not embedded in JSON backups. For iCloud photos on iOS, enable photo sync separately. Save a current backup before restoring and keep it in a private location; it can contain householder details. Use the Help Center’s private support option for recovery help.
faq_shareAddress_q: How do I get directions to a contact?
faq_shareAddress_a: Open the contact and tap their address. You'll be offered Apple Maps, Google Maps, or Waze depending on what's installed. You can also pin a contact's location without an address, which is useful for areas where street numbers don't exist.
faq_manualPin_q: My pin is in the wrong place. Can I move it?
faq_manualPin_a: Yes. Open the contact's address screen and drag the pin to the correct spot. You can also place a pin without an address at all, which is helpful in areas without precise geolocation data.
faq_profilePic_q: Can I add a photo to a contact?
faq_profilePic_a: Yes. Open a contact, tap the avatar, and pick a photo from your library or take a new one. This is especially handy when contacts share names or when a photo helps you spot the right door.
faq_dismissContact_q: How do I hide a contact without deleting them?
faq_dismissContact_a: Open the contact and tap "Dismiss." You'll pick how long to dismiss them for (1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, or 1 year). The contact disappears from your active lists for that period and then comes back automatically when the time is up. If notifications are enabled, you'll also get a reminder when they reappear, so dismissed contacts won't quietly slip through the cracks. You can find or restore dismissed contacts at any time under Settings → Dismissed Contacts.
faq_reportBug_q: How do I report a bug or request a feature?
faq_reportBug_a: Use the buttons below to report a bug or request a feature. Include the steps to reproduce it, what you expected, your device and operating-system version, and the WitnessWork version shown under Still need help?. Remove private contact details, notes, account IDs, and Buddies Codes or invite links from public reports and screenshots. For backup or other sensitive problems, use the private email link in Still need help? instead. Source code and known issues are linked there too.
faq_becomeSupporter_q: What do I get as a supporter?
faq_becomeSupporter_a: An active Supporter subscription gives you the Supporter badge and custom accent colors, plus iCloud Sync and alternate app icons on iOS. When Notes Import is available, its current free and Supporter allowances appear in Help and on the support screen. Core features remain free, including Buddies when available; Supporters can also choose each buddy's color. A one-time Tip gives Donor recognition but does not activate Supporter features.
faq_stillFree_a: Yes — and always will be. Every core feature stays free for everyone. Supporting is completely optional; it helps fund ongoing development and unlocks a few personal touches as a thank-you.
faq_stopSupporting_q: What happens if I stop supporting?
faq_stopSupporting_a: Your existing data and local backups remain available if you stop supporting. iCloud sync pauses while Supporter access is unavailable. If sync was on, it resumes when access returns; an explicit choice to turn it off stays off. Photo sync follows its own setting. Check Settings → iCloud Sync for the current status.
faq_acceptDonations_a: As a brother in the hall, I consider it a privilege to be able to use my skills to help others in the congregation. Although free to everyone, developing, running, and maintaining this application, unfortunately costs a significant amount of money and time. I view donating as similar to how one might pay for another's gas after going in service with them - it's a loving gesture that goes greatly appreciated.
faq_donationsUsedFor_q: What are the donations used for?
faq_donationsUsedFor_a: Your donation helps keeps this app running! There are costs with purchasing real devices as development equipment, paying for location API service fees, build service API fees, app store fees, and opportunity cost of my many hours spent developing this app. Each piece of support is greatly appreciated!
faq_whatsNew_q: Where can I see what changed in the latest update?
faq_findNavigation_q: Where are Map, Buddies, and Settings?
faq_findNavigation_a: The bottom bar shows Home, Schedule, Contacts, and Progress, with Add beside them for logging time, creating a Plan, or adding a contact. Progress and Add Time appear when your role logs hours. Map is inside Contacts: tap Map at the top of Contacts, and WitnessWork opens the view you used last. Buddies, when available on iOS, opens from the Buddies button at the top of Schedule. View Report at the top of Progress opens the Service Report for the month you're viewing. Tap your profile picture at the top left of any main screen for Profile (your role, time served, and stats), Settings, Support, and Help Center; on a wide tablet layout, Settings also stays in the sidebar. If you hid the sidebar, tap Show sidebar in the page header to bring it back. If you turned on Hide Donate Heart, Support is left out of that menu and stays in Settings. Your contacts, plans, and records are unchanged; only where you find them moved. If something still seems missing, update the app, then use Still need help? below.
faq_tabletSidebar_q: How do I resize or hide the sidebar on my tablet?
faq_tabletSidebar_a: On a wide tablet window on iOS or Android, drag the small bar halfway down the sidebar's right edge to resize it. Narrowing the sidebar hides destination names and leaves their icons; widen it to show the names again. Tap Hide sidebar beside WitnessWork (at the top of the icon-only sidebar) to hide navigation completely. Tap Show sidebar in the page header to restore your last saved width. Your width and visibility are saved on this device across app restarts; they are not synced or included in ministry backups, and resizing does not change your records. The sidebar needs a window at least 1,000 points wide and a supported text size. In a narrower window or with very large text, the bottom bar returns automatically; widen the window or rotate to landscape to use the sidebar again. Screen reader users can adjust the Resize sidebar control to increase or decrease its width. If the navigation still seems missing, restart the app and use Still need help? below; keep contact details and other private data out of public reports.
faq_whatsNew_a: Tap your profile picture, then Settings → What's New, for a summary of recent changes. Big updates also open a short tour the first time you launch after updating. If you choose Later, the notification bell keeps a shortcut to it, and What's New has a button to take the tour again.
faq_notificationsTray_q: What's in the bell on Home?
faq_notificationsTray_a: The bell at the top of Home collects reminders and updates, so they wait there instead of piling up on Home when you open the app. You'll find things like last month's Service Report, a pending time rollover, backup and data protection reminders, missed Follow-ups, reminders that already went off, Buddies activity (where Buddies is available), ready Notes Imports, and What's New. The red badge counts items you haven't seen yet. Tap an item to act on it, tap X to dismiss it, or tap Clear All. Invitations and requests still waiting for your answer stay until you respond. A dismissed item doesn't come back. Which items you've seen or dismissed is remembered on this device only.
faq_shareApp_q: How do I share WitnessWork with a friend?
faq_shareApp_a: Tap your profile picture, then Settings → Share WitnessWork. Pick Android or iPhone, and your friend can scan the code with their phone's camera to open WitnessWork in Google Play or the App Store. Share Link sends a message with both store links, so it works for anyone. WitnessWork is free on both. The message only contains the store links — nothing about you or your records. If a code won't scan, turn up your screen's brightness or use Share Link instead.
faq_android_a: Yes. WitnessWork is back on Google Play, and it's free. Time and reports, the timer, contacts and follow-ups, plans, the map (with Google Maps), mileage, reminders, and backups all work on Android. A few features rely on Apple services and stay on iPhone and iPad: iCloud Sync, widgets, Live Activities, app icons, Calendar Sync, Notes Import, and Buddies. To move to a new phone on either platform, create a backup (Settings → Backup & Restore → Create Backup), copy the file to the new phone, then choose From a backup file on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen. Keep backup files private; they can contain householder details.
faq_backupRecovery_q: My backup looks unreadable or my restored records are missing. What should I do?
faq_backupRecovery_a: A WitnessWork backup is structured JSON for the app to read, so it does not look like a printable Service Report. Keep the original file unchanged and restore it through Settings → Backup & Restore → Restore From Backup. If records are missing, preserve the original backup and create a separate backup of the device's current data before trying another restore. Email support with the app version and what happened; arrange any file sharing privately. Backup files can contain contact details and notes, so keep them out of public bug reports.
faq_syncTroubleshooting_q: My devices are not syncing. What can I check?
faq_syncTroubleshooting_a: On iOS, use the same Apple Account, turn on iCloud Drive, and enable WitnessWork under iCloud on each device. iCloud sync requires Supporter access. Open Settings → iCloud Sync and use Sync now. Changes waiting to be sent are retried; an unreadable file or newer app version is shown in the status, so update every device and try again. The status shows Uploading to iCloud until Apple confirms the upload, and Last synced counts only confirmed uploads. If your iCloud storage is full, changes stay on this device; free up space or upgrade your storage in Settings → [Your Name] → iCloud and uploading resumes on its own. Keep an exported backup and the device containing your latest data. Rebuild iCloud data replaces the iCloud data with this device’s data and removes iCloud photos it doesn’t use. Your other devices switch to that data the next time they sync, replacing changes made on them before then, and the Home bell notes it. Update WitnessWork on every device first: an older version keeps its own data until it is updated. Contact private support from the Help Center if syncing remains incomplete. Keep householder details out of public reports.
faq_syncPhotos_q: Why are contact photos missing on my other device?
faq_syncPhotos_a: Photo sync is an optional Supporter feature on iOS. Open Settings → iCloud Sync and turn on Include images in sync. This uploads profile and contact photos to your private iCloud container and downloads referenced photos; they count against iCloud storage. Update WitnessWork on every device to use photo revisions safely. Pausing photo sync on one device keeps the uploaded files and local copies. To remove uploaded photos, choose Remove iCloud photos and pause photo sync on other devices first, or they can upload their copies again. Removing a contact or its photo removes downloaded copies when that change arrives; obsolete cloud copies are cleaned up after a one-day grace period. If a photo is missing, keep the device with the original, check storage and permissions, then use Sync now. Use the Help Center’s private support option if it still fails; do not include householder information in public reports.
faq_mytimeTrouble_q: MyTime Import says the file is not a database. What should I use?
faq_mytimeTrouble_a: MyTime Import needs an original .mytimedb backup created by MyTime. A PDF, text export, WitnessWork JSON backup, or a file renamed to .mytimedb will not work. Save a complete copy of the MyTime backup on your device and select it through Settings → MyTime Import. Keep the original file unchanged. If a valid backup still fails, email support privately with the error and app version; do not post the backup in a public issue.
faq_notesImportHelp_q: How does Notes Import work, and what does it cost?
faq_notesImportHelp_a: When Notes Import is available on your supported iOS device, open it from Settings and paste readable ministry notes. Scribe AI proposes contacts, visits, and time entries; review the preview, assumptions, and warnings before saving selected records. The Help button explains what to include and shows the current free and Supporter allowances. Failed, cancelled, and repeated imports do not count toward the allowance. Your notes are sent to a language-model service under a Zero Data Retention arrangement; import history stays on this device. Find the OpenRouter ZDR policy under Still need help?, using the support button in this screen's header. Notes Import is unavailable on Android.
faq_notesImportRetry_q: Notes Import failed, is still working, or found no records. What should I do?
faq_notesImportRetry_a: Check your internet connection and follow any Update WitnessWork message. If an import is still working, reopen Notes Import and check its history before starting another copy. For too much text, use smaller batches; if Scribe AI cannot interpret it, add clear names, dates, and time spent, then retry. If the service is temporarily unavailable, try later. A preview with no records means nothing was found to import. Review the preview before saving, and email support privately if the error continues.
faq_hourglassSetup_q: How do I send my report to Hourglass or NW Publisher?
faq_hourglassSetup_a: Open the month's Service Report, choose Hourglass or NW Publisher in the dropdown above Submit, and tap Submit. Review and send the report in the destination app. Copy and Share are also available. NW Publisher accepts only the previous month's report. Hourglass receives preaching time separately, with Credit Time included in the default report comment; if you replace the comment, check that it still says what you need. Update WitnessWork if a submission option is missing.
faq_conversationFields_q: Can I track extra details on a conversation, like the publication I used?
faq_conversationFields_a: Yes. Open Preferences → Conversation Fields, or tap Add Custom Fields on the conversation form, and add a field such as Publication. Field names can be up to 14 characters. Every field appears on the form for conversations and Not at Home visits; leave it empty when it doesn't apply. Saved values show on that visit in the contact's history. You can rename and reorder fields any time without losing what you entered. Archiving a field hides it but keeps its values. Delete it from the Archived list to remove the field and its values from every conversation for good. Fields and values stay on your device, are included in backups, and sync between devices with iCloud Sync on iOS; update WitnessWork on each device to see them there. They aren't included when you share a contact. Contact fields are managed separately in Preferences → Contact Fields. With data protection mode on, don't record religion, health, family situation, language, or ethnicity. If a field is missing from the form, check whether it was archived. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_followUpReminders_q: Can I keep visit notes without scheduling a return visit or reminder?
faq_followUpReminders_a: Yes. When adding or editing a visit, turn off Follow Up and save. The visit and its notes remain, but that visit has no scheduled follow-up or reminder and will not appear as overdue. You can turn Follow Up on later and choose a date and time. To stop an older follow-up reminder, edit that visit and turn Follow Up off.
faq_followUpCard_q: How do I use the Today's Conversations card on Home?
faq_followUpCard_a: The card shows the follow-ups you scheduled for today. From 5 PM it shows Upcoming Conversations, which adds tomorrow's; those can be rescheduled but not logged until their day. Swipe sideways to move between people. When you've been, tap Talked to log the conversation in the visit form, or tap Not at Home to log the attempt right away. Undo appears below the card for a few seconds after Not at Home. The calendar button reschedules the follow-up. Use the ••• button or touch and hold a person for call, message, directions, and Dismiss Follow-Up. A follow-up counts as done once you log any visit with that person on or after its day. The bar at the top fills as you go, and the card shows All caught up when every one is done. Tap Done, or touch and hold the title and choose Close for Now, to hide the card until you add or reschedule a follow-up. A follow-up still open 4 hours after its time moves to missed follow-ups in the notifications tray. Not at Home is unavailable while data protection mode is on. Visits are saved like any other visit on this device. To remove the card for good, touch and hold its title and choose Hide This Section, or turn it back on in Customize Home. If something looks wrong, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_reminders_q: How do follow-up, plan, and contact reminders work?
faq_reminders_a: Turn on Notify Me when adding or editing a Follow-up or a one-time Plan, then choose how long before it starts the reminder should arrive. Dismissing a contact also reminds you when they're available again. If Notify Me is off because notifications aren't allowed, turning it on asks for permission; if you've declined before, it opens your device settings. If the reminder time has already passed, the form says so and no reminder is sent. Rescheduling keeps the reminder time you chose. When a reminder arrives, it is also listed in the Home bell, even if system notifications are off, and tapping either one opens the follow-up, plan, or contact. Each device schedules its own reminders from your saved records, so after iCloud sync or a backup restore, open WitnessWork once on that device to set them up. Deleting a visit, plan, or contact removes its reminders, including any already shown. With data protection mode on, reminders leave out names and topics. On Android, the system may deliver a reminder a few minutes late to save battery. If reminders don't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in Preferences and in your device settings, and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.
faq_appIconBadge_q: Why is there a number on the WitnessWork app icon?
faq_appIconBadge_a: On iOS, the number on the app icon is how many items in the Home notification bell you haven't read yet. Open the bell and scroll through it to mark items read; dismissing or clearing them also lowers the number. It updates while WitnessWork is open and when a Follow-up, Plan, or contact reminder arrives. Other items, like last month's report or Buddies activity, are counted the next time you open WitnessWork, so the number can be behind while the app is closed. Each device keeps its own count. The number needs notification permission; to hide it, turn off Badges for WitnessWork in your device's notification settings. On Android, the app icon doesn't show an unread count; your launcher may show a dot for notifications in the notification shade. If the number looks wrong, open WitnessWork, then leave it to refresh the count. If it still doesn't match the bell, contact support from the Help Center.
faq_soundEffects_q: How do I turn off celebration and reminder sounds?
faq_soundEffects_a: Open Settings → Preferences → Audio & Haptics and turn off Play sounds. This controls celebration chimes and reminders while WitnessWork is open; reminders still appear, just without sound (on Android, as a short message in the app). Reminders received while the app is closed follow your device's notification settings; adjust those separately if needed.
faq_haptics_q: How do I turn off vibrations?
faq_haptics_a: Open Settings → Preferences → Audio & Haptics and turn off Haptics. WitnessWork then stops all of its vibration feedback, such as taps, chart scrubbing, and goal celebrations. The setting applies only to this device and isn't synced to your other devices. Some system controls, like menus and switches, may still vibrate based on your device's own settings; adjust those in your device's sound and haptics settings.
faq_locationTrouble_q: Why can't the map find my current location?
faq_locationTrouble_a: Check that location services are on and WitnessWork has location permission in your device's settings. Reopen the map and try again where your device can obtain a location. You can still enter an address or place a contact's pin manually without using your current location. If the problem continues, report the error with your device and operating-system version, leaving private contact details out of screenshots.
faq_restoreSupporter_q: I already paid, but Supporter features or prices are missing. What should I do?
faq_restoreSupporter_a: Check your connection and that your device's store uses the account you purchased with. Open Settings → Become a supporter and use Restore Purchases when it is shown. A one-time Tip does not activate Supporter features. If no purchases are found, prices do not load, or your subscription still is not recognized, email support privately with your app version and what happened. If support needs your account ID, use the support button in this screen's header to open Still need help?, then tap Copy Account ID. Share that ID privately. Restoring purchases restores access, not your service records.
faq_buddiesOverview_q: What is WitnessWork Buddies, and why don't I see it?
faq_buddiesOverview_a: Buddies lets you connect with up to five people you go out in service with and see each other's planned days, start times, and durations for the next eight weeks. It is free when available. Open Schedule, tap Buddies at the top, and complete the introduction with your profile name. A dot on that button means a request is waiting for you to confirm. Buddies currently requires a supported iOS build and may be unavailable during rollout. Update the installed app if the Buddies button is missing. Buddies is not currently available on Android.
faq_buddiesAdd_q: How do I add a buddy, and who confirms the request?
faq_buddiesAdd_a: Open Buddies and tap Invite a Buddy or the + button to share a Buddies Invite. To pair in person, use the code button to show your Buddies Code and have the other person scan it inside WitnessWork. You can also paste a link through Enter Invite Link. The recipient taps Accept; the person who created the invite then opens Buddies → Requests and taps Confirm. You start seeing each other's plans only after that confirmation. Confirm only the person you intended to invite.
faq_buddiesInviteTrouble_q: Why is my Buddies Invite waiting, expired, or saying all spots are in use?
faq_buddiesInviteTrouble_a: An accepted request waits until the inviter confirms it in Buddies → Requests. Each Buddies Invite works once and expires after seven days; ask for a new link if it was used, cancelled, or expired. Your five spots include buddies and pending invites or requests. Cancel an unused invite or remove a buddy to make room. Only a limited number of unused invite links can be open at once. If scanning is unavailable, allow camera access in your device's settings or share and paste the invite link instead.
faq_buddiesPrivacy_q: What can my buddies see, and is sharing private?
faq_buddiesPrivacy_a: Automatic calendar sharing includes your name and planned days, start times, and durations for the next eight weeks. Photo and pioneer status are optional; change them in Buddies Settings. This calendar sharing does not include your recorded service time, reports, goals, categories, contact list, visit history, or notes. Shared content is end-to-end encrypted so only you and the buddies you choose can read it. Explicit Plan and Follow-up invitations share extra details, including a Plan's note or a Follow-up's address; check those details before inviting someone. Find the Privacy Policy under Still need help?, using the support button in this screen's header.
faq_buddiesInvitations_q: How do I invite a buddy to a Plan or Follow-up, and answer an invitation?
faq_buddiesInvitations_a: Use Invite Buddies when adding or editing a Plan or scheduled Follow-up, select confirmed buddies, and save. You can also tap Invite to a Plan on a buddy's page. A Plan invite shares its date, time, duration, title, location, and note. A Follow-up invite shares its date/time, the householder's first name, address or pin, and topic; those details expire a day after the visit. Check that you want to share these details with the people selected. Follow-up invitations are unavailable in Data Protection Mode. To reply, open the notification bell on Home or the buddy's page in Buddies and choose Going or Can't Make It; you can change your answer later. An invitation stays in the bell until you answer it or it is canceled or expires, so it can't be dismissed or cleared by mistake; once answered, you can dismiss it. Going to a Plan adds a linked Plan to your schedule, which follows the inviter's changes or cancellation. A Follow-up invite does not import the contact or visit history.
faq_buddiesDetail_q: What's on a buddy's page, and can I rename them or change their color?
faq_buddiesDetail_a: Open Buddies and tap a buddy. Needs your answer lists their invitations you haven't answered; choose Going or Can't Make It there or in the Home notification bell. Together lists upcoming Plans and Follow-ups between you two, whoever invited whom, with each answer; use the menu on a buddy's invitation to change your answer. Next two weeks shows the days your buddy plans to go out next to your own; tap one of their days to plan the same time. Invite to a Plan opens a new Plan with that buddy already invited, and View on Calendar opens Schedule. A nickname is a private name only you see; your buddy isn't told, and clearing it brings back their own name. Choosing a buddy's color is a Supporter feature; everyone else keeps the color given when you paired. Nicknames and colors are kept with your encrypted Buddies data, so they return when Buddies restores on another device. Their full schedule for the next eight weeks is on your calendar while Show on my calendar is on.
faq_buddiesMissingPlans_q: Why are a buddy's plans or invitations missing or out of date?
faq_buddiesMissingPlans_a: Check that the request has been confirmed and Show on my calendar is on for that buddy. Calendar sharing covers only the next eight weeks. Both people need an internet connection to send and receive changes; open Buddies and pull down to refresh or tap Refresh Buddies. Previously downloaded plans remain viewable offline, but new changes need a connection. Seeing a buddy's calendar does not add their plans to yours. Turn on Buddies notifications in Buddies Settings and your device's notification settings, and check the Home notification bell for invitations even if no notification arrived. The bell checks for new Buddies activity when you open it and when you return to WitnessWork; if it says it couldn't check, reconnect and tap Try Again.
faq_buddiesRemove_q: How do I hide a buddy, stop sharing, or delete my Buddies data?
faq_buddiesRemove_a: Open a buddy's details and turn off Show on my calendar to hide their plans on this device; sharing continues. Remove Buddy ends the connection for both people, and reconnecting takes a new invite. They are not notified, though they may notice. If removal is pending while offline, they may still see your last shared plans until WitnessWork reconnects and completes it. Buddies Settings → Delete My Buddies Data removes all connections and invites and erases your encrypted Buddies data and encryption identity. It cannot be undone; reconnect and retry if deletion is pending. Your personal service records and contacts remain.
faq_buddiesRestore_q: Can I recover my buddies on another device or from a backup?
faq_buddiesRestore_a: On a supported iOS device using the same Apple Account with your Buddies encryption key available through iCloud Keychain, Buddies can restore its connections when it syncs. Regular WitnessWork backup files do not contain that encryption key. Buddies recovery is separate from Supporter iCloud Sync for service records. If the key is unavailable, or you used Delete My Buddies Data, reconnect with new invites. Keep your personal records backed up separately.
faq_mileageStart_a: Mileage Tracking is optional and available for every publisher type. Answer Yes on the "Track mileage?" card on Home, or turn on Track Mileage in Settings → Preferences → Publisher. Then add your first car; only a name is required. Log a trip with Log Trip on Home's Mileage card, from the Add button, or on the Mileage screen. Enter the distance (turn on Round Trip to double it) or switch to Odometer and enter start and end readings. Odometer Start fills in from that car's last reading. Trips can't be dated in the future. Tap a trip to see its details, or long-press it to edit, log it again today, share, or delete it.
faq_mileageCost_q: How is the estimated fuel cost calculated, and what happens when fuel prices change?
faq_mileageCost_a: Estimated fuel cost is distance ÷ the car's fuel economy × its fuel's price, using the values in effect on each trip's date. It only appears once the car has a fuel economy and its fuel has a price; trips without both are left out and the report says so. A fuel's price is shared by every car that uses that fuel. When you change a price or a car's fuel economy, choose From a Date to apply it from that day forward (earlier trips keep the old value) or Fix Current Value to correct a mistake, which also updates the past trips that used it. Each fuel and car keeps a history; long-press an entry to delete it. The amount is only an estimate. If you're reimbursed, the actual amount is calculated by whoever reimburses you.
faq_mileageUnits_q: Can I use kilometers, litres, or L/100 km?
faq_mileageUnits_a: Yes. Open Mileage → Settings (the gear) → Units. Distance can be miles or kilometers, and fuel economy can be mpg (US), mpg (UK), L/100 km, or km/L. Auto follows your device's region. Fuel is priced per gallon with mpg (US) and per litre with every other choice. Currency follows your device's region. Changing units only changes how numbers are shown; your trips aren't altered.
faq_mileageShare_q: How do I share or export my mileage report?
faq_mileageShare_a: Open Mileage, choose Day, Week, Month, or Year (service year, September to August), and use the arrows or swipe to pick the period. Tap the share button at the top to Copy the report, Share it as text, or Export CSV for a spreadsheet. The text lists totals, per-car totals when you have more than one car, and each trip except in the Year view. The CSV has one row per trip with the car, odometer readings, distance, note, fuel, fuel economy, price, and estimated cost. Trip notes are included, so check them before sending. To share one trip, open it and tap the share button.
faq_mileageCars_q: What's the difference between archiving and deleting a car?
faq_mileageCars_a: Open Mileage → Settings, tap the car, and choose Archive or Delete…. Archiving hides the car from new trips but keeps its trips in your reports; unarchive it anytime from Archived Cars. Deleting removes the car and all of its trips on every device that syncs with this one, and can't be undone. Deleting a fuel removes its price history, so cars using it stop showing an estimated cost.
faq_mileageSync_q: Does my mileage sync, and does it work on Android?
faq_mileageSync_a: Mileage works on iOS and Android. Cars, fuels, prices, and trips sync between iOS devices with iCloud Sync, which is a Supporter feature, and they're included in backups from Settings → Backup & Restore on both platforms. iCloud Sync isn't available on Android, so use a backup to move your mileage between devices. Mileage is never shared with Buddies and doesn't appear on your calendar or Service Report.
faq_mileageTurnOff_q: How do I turn mileage tracking on or off?
faq_mileageChart_q: What does the chart on the Mileage screen show?
faq_mileageChart_a: Open the Mileage screen and choose Week, Month, or Year. The chart shows how far you drove each day, or each month of the service year (September through August). When more than one car has trips in that period, each bar is split by car, using the colors next to each car's total. Tap a bar to open that day or month and see its trips. The Day view has no chart, and a period without trips shows none. Bars show distance, not estimated cost.
faq_mileageTurnOff_a: Use the Track Mileage switch in Settings → Preferences → Publisher. Turning it off hides the Home card, the Log Trip action, and the Mileage screen, but keeps your trips; turn it back on and everything returns. If you chose No Thanks on the Home card, this switch turns it on anytime. To erase your mileage, open Mileage → Settings → Delete All Mileage Data. This deletes it on every device that syncs with this one and can't be undone. You can also hide only the Home card with Settings → Preferences → Home Screen.

faq_syncRecovery_q: What happens to setup choices, deleted contacts, and reminders during sync?
faq_syncRecovery_a: Restart onboarding affects only this device. Choosing Set up fresh pauses iCloud sync until you explicitly enable it in Settings; then choose Merge both or Restore from iCloud as appropriate. Restore from iCloud reads other devices’ snapshots and replaces local data after confirmation. During onboarding, a device that already has records asks before replacing them, and Supporters can choose Merge instead. Keep this device’s data makes your other devices switch to this device’s data the next time they sync, replacing changes made on them before then. Restoring data does not send Buddies declines for plans absent from the backup. Recoverable deleted contact details are retained for up to 90 days, then removed while deletion evidence remains. Reminders are rebuilt on this device after merges and restores, keeping the reminder time chosen for each follow-up and plan; notification permission is required and only future reminders are scheduled. For recovery, keep the device with the latest records and export a backup before replacing data. Use private Help Center support if you need help.
faq_syncRemoveDevice_q: How do I remove an old device from iCloud sync?
faq_syncRemoveDevice_a: Each device that uses iCloud Sync keeps its own copy of your data in your iCloud, and that copy stays after you stop using the device, even after a reinstall or a new phone. Remove it when you no longer use a device, for example one you sold, replaced, or reset. On a device that still syncs, open Settings → iCloud Sync → Devices and tap Remove beside the old device. Devices not synced in 90 or more days are marked. Removing deletes only that device’s copy from iCloud, including details it still held of contacts deleted elsewhere. This device keeps everything it has already synced, and your other devices aren’t changed. If the removed device is still in use, it adds its data back the next time it syncs; turn off iCloud Sync on it first if you want it to stop. Before removing a device, this device must finish syncing its data; if asked, go back, tap Sync now, and fix any problem the status shows. If the device uses a newer version of WitnessWork, update this device first. Devices replaced by Rebuild iCloud data can be removed at any time. Photos aren’t stored per device, so removing a device doesn’t remove photos; use Remove iCloud photos for that. Devices is part of iCloud Sync, a Supporter feature on iOS only. If you need help, use the Help Center’s private support option and keep householder details out of public reports.
